title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launches ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan’ in Andaman & Nicobar Islands
subtitle:
Vice-President says Andaman & Nicobar Islands are a sacred land of sacrifice and an eternal symbol of India’s freedom struggle
“Bharat is one and will always remain one”: Vice-President
Vice-President says Great Nicobar Development Project will strengthen India’s maritime capabilities and unlock new opportunities for growth
Vice President calls upon every citizen to proudly display the Tricolour and uphold its values of courage, unity and patriotism
body_text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan’ by hoisting the National Flag at Flag Point, Sri Vijaya Puram, on the occasion of August Kranti Diwas, commemorating the Quit India Movement of 1942.
Hoisted the National Flag at Flag Point, Sri Vijaya Puram, today under the #HarGharTiranga Abhiyaan, a historic site where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Tricolour on December 30, 1943, proclaiming the Andaman & Nicobar Islands free from British rule. On Quit India… pic.twitter.com/vA8x5wLNzW — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 9, 2026
Addressing the gathering at the State Function and Tiranga Concert on Vande Mataram at the DBRAIT Auditorium, the Vice-President said there could be no more appropriate place to launch the campaign than these historic islands, which are deeply associated with India’s freedom struggle and the history of the Tricolour.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the State Function on ‘Har Ghar Tiranga - Dedicated to the Spirit of Vande Mataram’ at the DBRAIT Auditorium, in Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman & Nicobar Islands today. The Vice-President said there could be no more appropriate place to… pic.twitter.com/T6YDjhHWxU — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 9, 2026
Recalling the immortal words of the great Tamil poet Subramania Bharati, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Bharati’s celebration of the ‘Mani Kodi’ reflects the eternal courage of the Indian spirit and the glory of the flag of Mother Bharat. He said the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan carries forward this spirit by bringing every citizen together under one National Flag, one motherland and one common destiny. Recalling the sacrifices of freedom fighters who endured the dreaded Kala Pani, the Vice President said the Andaman & Nicobar Islands are much more than a geographical part of Bharat; they are a sacred land of sacrifice. He paid heartfelt tributes to Veer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and countless other patriots who suffered in the Cellular Jail, saying their courage, patriotism and sacrifice continue to inspire generations. The Vice-President recalled that Mahatma Gandhi’s clarion call of “Do or Die” on August 8, 1942, awakened millions of Indians and gave a decisive impetus to the freedom struggle. He also highlighted the unique place of the islands in the history of the Tricolour, recalling that Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian National Flag here on December 30, 1943, marking a landmark moment in India’s freedom struggle. Highlighting the significance of Har Ghar Tiranga, Shri Radhakrishnan said the campaign, initiated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has evolved into a nationwide people’s movement. He called upon every citizen to proudly display the Tricolour and imbibe the values of patriotism, unity and collective responsibility that it represents. “Bharat is one and will always remain one,” he affirmed. The Vice-President highlighted the islands as a living example of ‘Unity in Diversity’ and ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’, while acknowledging their rich tribal heritage and recent progress in connectivity, healthcare, education and infrastructure. He said the Great Nicobar Island Development Project would further strengthen India’s maritime capabilities, connectivity and economic opportunities, while balancing development with environmental conservation. Emphasising the need for national strength alongside India’s tradition of peace and generosity, Shri Radhakrishnan said, “India has always been generous, but our generosity should never be mistaken for weakness. We must remain prepared to protect our national interests and sovereignty.” He called upon citizens to let the Tricolour inspire them with courage, unity and hope, and to carry forward the legacy of the freedom fighters in building a stronger and developed Bharat. The Vice-President also attended a cultural programme and visited the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ Exhibition, showcasing the spirit of the campaign and its message of national unity and patriotism. The event was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Andaman & Nicobar Islands Admiral D. K. Joshi (Retd.), Chief Secretary Smt. Chanchal Yadav, Chairperson of Sri Vijaya Puram Municipal Council Smt. M. Vasantha and Adhyaksh, Zilla Parishad, Shri P. Ummer, among other dignitaries.

enrichment.summary: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the 'Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan' by hoisting the National Flag at Flag Point, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, on August Kranti Diwas (August 9, 2026), marking the anniversary of the 1942 Quit India Movement. He addressed a State Function at DBRAIT Auditorium, invoking the islands' freedom struggle legacy including Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's 1943 flag-hoisting and the sacrifices at Cellular Jail, and spoke about the Great Nicobar Island Development Project strengthening India's maritime capabilities.
enrichment.context:
The Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan, launched by the Government of India in 2022 as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, encourages citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes to foster patriotism and awareness of the Indian flag's significance; it has since become an annual campaign around Independence Day. The choice of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands as the launch site is symbolically significant: the islands housed the Cellular Jail where freedom fighters including Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were imprisoned, and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Tricolour there in December 1943 after declaring the islands liberated under the Azad Hind Government, making it one of the earliest instances of Indian sovereignty being asserted on Indian soil.

The reference to the Great Nicobar Island Development Project ties into ongoing debates about India's strategic and economic push in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, including a proposed international container transshipment terminal, airport, and township aimed at bolstering India's presence in the Indian Ocean Region and countering China's growing maritime influence, while raising environmental and tribal rights concerns due to the region's ecological sensitivity and indigenous population (e.g., Shompen tribe). This event also reflects the government's broader messaging on national unity, 'Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat', and assertive foreign/strategic policy posture.

prelims_questions.question: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian National Flag in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, declaring them free from British rule, on which date?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Tricolour at Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) on December 30, 1943, proclaiming the islands free from British rule under the Azad Hind Government.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan' mentioned in the release was originally launched as part of which government initiative?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan was initiated under the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorating 75/other milestone years of India's independence, encouraging citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes.
